health development levels can be used to identify health status determinants and to develop health systems models that can be used in policy formulation.

the health status of a nation is a function of economic, political, educational, social, and other health determinators, but that these determinators vary systematically with the level of health development of the nation.
the health status of a country is determined in large part by its level of health development and the health status of other countries.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of a new tool, levels of health development, for comparative research and health policy formulation.

the relationship between health status and social development, the role of health determinants and their relative importance at different levels of development, and the implications for health policy formulation.
the relationship between social systems and health status.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
health status in countries is determined by a set of factors, each of which plays a different role in different countries, depending on the level of health development of the country.
levels of health development are an important tool for comparative health research and policy formulation.
health development levels are the most appropriate tool currently available for comparative health research and health policy formulation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
levels of health development provide an effective tool for comparative research.
levels of health development are an effective tool to delineate the relative importance of economic, health, and other social determinants of health status.
health status is not a random variable.
The main takeaway from our work is that

health development levels can be used to delineate the relative importance of economic, health, education, political, and demographic health determinants, thereby facilitating the formulation of more effective health policy and more accurate comparative research.

the way health determinants are identified and prioritized should be dependent on the health development level of a particular country, and that the health development level is a critical variable that should be considered by health policy analysts and policymakers.
health status is not a function of economic development, but of the way in which a country's social systems have developed.
